reviewBasis.method: Read-only source and Git inspection, complete archived-log scanning, diagnostic-patch inspection, in-memory gzip decompression and checksum verification. Execution results below belong to the retained implementation runs; I did not rerun them.
reviewBasis.scope: The complete 58-file original-base-to-implementation change, including ticket updates and evidence artifacts; the shared EPUB helper's 23 importing test files; relevant save, storage, admission and restoration paths; all retained current and historical execution logs.
reviewBasis.instructions: Read AGENTS.md, docs/plans/bookfin.md, both requested tickets, reviewer.md, software-design/SKILL.md and reviewer-brief.md. No CLAUDE.md was present in the worktree.
reviewBasis.restrictionsObserved: No edits, commits, builds, tests, formatting, analyzer execution, evidence/run.py execution, delegates, device/browser actions or integration actions.

evidence.assessment: The only final test-code change assigns a fixed modification time to every archive entry, including entries supplied through extra. Payload construction, entry order and caller arguments remain unchanged. Inspection of archive 4.0.9 confirms that ZIP encoding uses this modification time as local calendar fields with two-second resolution.

The restart test remains byte-identical to the original base. Its two sessions independently admit archives built by epub(). FailingWrites awaits MemoryResume.saveReading; MemoryResume applies the changes to its account map.

The controlled two-second difference produces two 1440-byte archives with matching hashes for all seven entry payloads but different archive digests. The delegated save completed, the stored location was present and saveFailed was false. Reopening rejected the different source digest, and the original assertion failed with the expected location versus null.
The identical diagnostic patch with a zero-second difference produces equal archive digests and publication identities. The saved location restores and the selected test passes.

The bounded negative control omits only the store.saveReading call. With the fixed fixture and unchanged restart test, the same assertion fails. Subsequent source snapshots match the final fixture-only patch.

Source-digest, policy and engine compatibility checks remain unchanged. The existing changed-content test in test/reader/session_test.dart:158 still rejects the old location and retains its bookmark. Production, account guards, pending-write handling and flush semantics have no base-to-head changes.

All six commits named in prerequisites-preserved.json are ancestors of the reviewed HEAD. Production, unread_records_test.dart and page_source_frames_test.dart remain unchanged.

evidence.assessment: The bug class is archive identity changing because fixture metadata depends on the clock. The existing shared builder now owns stable metadata for every entry it constructs. Both independent session loads retain the same model of source identity.

evidence.source: Ousterhout, software-design section 6: information hiding and pulling complexity downward
evidence.assessment: Callers need no timestamp parameter, shared-publication cache or special restoration rule. The fixture absorbs the metadata requirement, while production remains the owner of source compatibility and retained records.

The fix preserves the existing helper interface and adds no speculative abstraction, global counter or parallel mechanism. The diagnostic timestamp control is absent from final code. The evidence recorder is explicitly ticket-local tooling and introduces no application dependency.
